newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waterford, Avonmore in giant Irish food merger.
newsitem.headline: Waterford, Avonmore in giant Irish food merger.

text.p: Ireland's Waterford Foods said Tuesday it had agreed to improved merger terms from Avonmore Foods Plc to create a dairy giant which would be one of the five biggest milk producers in the world.

The agreement was reached at a marathon overnight meeting of the boards of Waterford Foods Plc and its associated farmers' cooperative in the southern town of Dungarvan, and will be put to shareholders and coop members for approval, a joint statement by Waterford and Avonmore said.
Avonmore's improved offer values the company at 337 million Irish pounds ($512 million) against an original offer of 281 million ($427 million), the statement said.
If approved, it will weld together two of Ireland's premier food companies with joint revenues of 2.5 billion pounds ($3.8 billion) and pretax profits of 71.5 million ($108.7 million).
This would create the largest dairy company in Britain and Ireland and the fourth largest milk processor in the world.
But some analysts said the planned merger could still fail due to a lack of support from farmers.
To succeed, the merger must be ratified by 75 percent of Waterford Coop, which owns 68 percent of the Plc shares, and Waterford Foods Plc members.

Under the proposal, Waterford Foods Plc shares will be valued at 142 pence ($2.158) compared with a closing price of 110 pence ($1.67) on the Dublin stock exchange Monday night and 80 pence ($1.216) before Waterford said it had been approached by Avonmore last month.
Avonmore's previous offer in April was rejected by Waterford as inadequate.

The two companies have interests in Europe, Britain and America. Avonmore is Ireland's single biggest dairy company with interests in meat products, animal foodstuffs and agricultural products including grain.
It has processing operations in Ireland, Britain, Belgium and the United States, Japan, Korea and Singapore.
Waterford is engaged in dairy-based food products, fruit juices and animal foodstuffs and has processing plants in Ireland, Britain and America.
